empty.help: A project is a folder with a git repository of scripts. Its files open in the editor and run on the database you choose; git keeps the history.

link.title: Link project
link.alreadyLinked: That folder is already linked as “{{name}}”.
link.useRoot: The repository root will be linked: {{root}}
link.hasManifest: It has a .dbine.json file with environments: you will then choose which database each one uses.
link.notRepo: The folder is not a git repository.
link.init: Initialize a git repository in the folder
link.name: Name in DBine

clone.title: Clone repository
clone.pickTitle: Choose where to clone the repository
clone.name: Folder name
clone.credentials: Git uses your own credentials (the credential helper or your SSH key). DBine neither asks for nor stores them.

base.label: Active database
base.missingEnv: Environment “{{env}}” no longer exists: choose another
base.pickLead: The files in “{{name}}” run on this connection and database. This applies to this machine only: it is not saved in the repository.
base.assignTitle: Assign this database to which environment?
base.assignLead: {{target}} is not the database of any environment in “{{name}}”. Choose which one to assign it to; that environment becomes active.

banner.noGit: Git is required to see changes, commit and sync. Install git (git-scm.com) and reopen DBine.
banner.missing: The project folder was not found. If you moved it, point to where it is now.
banner.notRepo: The folder is no longer a git repository.
banner.initAsk: A new git repository will be created in {{path}}. The files are not touched.
banner.manifestError: The .dbine.json file is not valid ({{error}}); the project uses a direct database.

files.title: Files
files.deleteFileAsk: Delete “{{name}}”? Versioned files can be recovered with git.
files.deleteFolderAsk: Delete the folder “{{name}}” and everything in it? Versioned files can be recovered with git.

changes.nothing: There are no changes to commit
changes.truncated: There are too many changes: only the first 5000 are shown.

conflicts.allResolved: The conflicts are resolved: Continue finishes the operation.
conflicts.finishFirst: Finish or abort the operation in progress first
conflicts.rebaseCommit: A rebase is in progress: continue or abort it

git.detachedTip: Detached HEAD: switch to a branch from git
git.noRemoteTip: The repository has no remote: Add remote…
git.busy: A git operation is in progress ({{op}})

menu.renameLabel: Name in DBine (the folder does not change)
menu.relocateTitle: Where is the folder of “{{name}}” now?

confirm.unlink: DBine stops showing “{{name}}”. The folder {{path}} and its files are not touched.
confirm.discardOne: Discard the changes to “{{name}}”? The file goes back to how it was in the last commit (if it is new, it is deleted).
confirm.abort: The repository goes back to how it was before the operation. What you resolved is lost.
confirm.saveBeforePull_one: “{{list}}” has unsaved changes. It must be saved before pulling changes from the remote.
confirm.saveBeforePull_other: {{count}} files have unsaved changes ({{list}}). They must be saved before pulling changes from the remote.
confirm.saveBeforePull_many: {{count}} files have unsaved changes ({{list}}). They must be saved before pulling changes from the remote.

envs.title: Environments of “{{name}}”
envs.lead: Environments are saved in the repository's .dbine.json file and shared with the team. Each person chooses, on their own machine, which connection and database to use for each one.
envs.name: Project name
envs.confirmRunTip: Ask for confirmation before each run in this environment
envs.defaultTip: The environment that is active when the project is linked
envs.noCredentials: The file never carries users, passwords or servers: only names.

problem.name: Environment names use letters, numbers, “_”, “.” or “-” (up to 40).
problem.duplicate: Two environments have the same name.

identity.title: Your name and email for git
identity.lead: Git signs every commit with a name and an email, and it doesn't have them set yet.
identity.name: Name
identity.global: Use them in all my repositories (global git configuration)

file.envTip: Environment “{{env}}”: click to change its database
file.followProjectTip: This tab chose another database: go back to the project's active database
file.extMismatchTip: .{{ext}} files are not usually {{engine}} files. It can still be run.
file.projectGone: The project is no longer linked: the file can't be saved from here.
file.confirmRun: You are about to run on “{{env}}” ({{where}}).

diff.binary: This is a binary file: its changes are not shown.
diff.tooLarge: The file is too large to show its changes.
diff.noChanges: This file no longer has uncommitted changes.

tabs.stayed: “{{name}}” stays on the previous database until the run finishes or the transaction is closed.
